newsitem.title: CHINA: China state bank stock ban to stop irregularities.
newsitem.headline: China state bank stock ban to stop irregularities.

text.p: China's move to stop funds from state banks from flowing into the stock markets was aimed at effectively checking widespread irregularities, an official newspaper said on Friday.

The measures unveiled on Thursday were taken after bank funds had flowed illegally into the stock markets, seriously damaging the interests of ordinary investors and disturbing the financial order, the Financial News, mouthpiece of the the People's Bank, the central bank, said in an editorial.
The central bank on Thursday issued an urgent notice banning state banks from trading on the stock markets and from the state debt repurchase and spot secondary markets.

"Investigations have found some securities organisations and enterprises, including listed firms, collaborated with some banks to speculate on the stock markets using bank money for illegal profits," the editorial said.
"A handful of commercial (state) banks and their branches had directly bought shares using bank money or offer credit for securities brokerages to bid new shares," it said.
Some listed companies had made use of bank loans to speculate on stock markets or trade for short-term profit on the state debt repurchase market, it said.
The newspaper said such irregularities had introduced stock market risk into the banking system and were endangering the whole financial system.
